## Purpose
The process-knowledge API, used by the Processes page, the Settings template section and the upload and picker on the orchestration pages. It manages the industry → domain → subdomain → process → subprocess tree, JSON process documents filed under processes (versioned, validated against scoped templates, with AI fix and draft), the templates themselves, document usage, and goal → process resolution.

## Responsibilities
- **`GET /processes/config`** returns `{default_enabled, max_kb, min_score, template{id, name, version}, levels}`.
- **Tree:**
  - `GET /processes/tree` returns the domain concepts (excluding `domain.system` and its children) and the process concepts. Each process carries `domain_id` (from the `part_of_domain` links), `documents` counts (total, valid, invalid, stale, active_id, active_version) and `usage` (agents, workflows, last_used).
  - `GET /processes/industries` returns one card per root industry. Counts cover domains, subdomains, processes, subprocesses, documents, valid documents, needs_attention (invalid plus stale), agents and workflows, plus last_used. Cards are sorted by label.
- **Concepts:**
  - **`POST /processes/concepts`** (201) takes `NodeCreate{level, label ≤120, parent_id, definition, synonyms, id?}`. The ids it generates:
    - industry: `domain.<slug>`;
    - domain or subdomain: `<parent>.<slug>`. The parent must be an industry (for a domain) or a domain (for a subdomain);
    - process: `process.<parent minus "domain.">.<slug>` in the process scheme, linked to its domain or subdomain. It cannot be filed directly under an industry, and if linking fails the concept is rolled back;
    - subprocess: `<parent process>.<slug>`.
    - Slugs are lower-case `[a-z0-9_]`, at most 48 characters. `_unique_id` appends `_2`, `_3` and so on.
  - **`GET /processes/concepts/{id}`** returns the node:
    - `children` and a breadcrumb `path`;
    - for processes: `domain_id`, `documents` and `usage` (up to 200);
    - for domains: the `processes` under it;
    - `usage_counts` and `template` (the template that applies there).
  - **`PATCH`** takes `{label, definition, synonyms, domain_id}`. `domain_id` moves a top-level process to another domain and is refused for anything else.
  - **`DELETE ?cascade=`** also runs `forget_concepts_in_neo4j`.
- **Documents:**
  - `POST /processes/concepts/{id}/documents` (multipart, with optional `template_id` and `replace_id`).
  - `POST .../documents/json` with `DocumentJson{content, filename, source, replace_id, template_id}`. Sources are upload, ai_fixed, ai_drafted or orchestration.
  - `POST /processes/documents` is an upload from an orchestration page. With `concept_id` it is filed there. Otherwise it stays unfiled and is checked against the template of where it is classified: `classify_as`, else what the document names, else the request `goal` (see `process.classifier`).
  - `POST /processes/documents/json` does the same from content.
  - `POST /processes/validate` checks a file without storing it, against an explicit template, the concept's template, or the classified template.
  - `POST /processes/classify` returns `{classification, template summary}`.
  - `GET /processes/documents?concept_id&unfiled`.
  - `GET /processes/documents/{id}` adds `path`, or "Unfiled upload".
  - `GET .../download` serves `<slug>_v<n>.json`.
  - `PUT /processes/documents/{id}` re-uploads. A valid document is never overwritten; its re-upload becomes a new version. An unfiled document keeps its stored classification.
  - `POST .../activate`, `POST .../file {concept_id}`, and `DELETE ?force=` (refused while in use unless forced).
- **AI:**
  - `POST /processes/fix` takes `FixRequest{document_id | raw, concept_id, template_id, goal, classify_as}` and calls `process.ai.fix(client, raw, template, concept_id)`. A stored unfiled document is fixed towards the template it was checked against.
  - `POST /processes/draft` takes `DraftRequest{text 20–60000, concept_id, template_id, classify_as}` and calls `ai.draft`.
  - Failures of either become 502 "The AI fix/draft could not be completed: …".
- **Templates.** Templates are scoped: a document is checked against the nearest active template above it (subprocess, process, subdomain, domain, industry, then global). `global` and `default` in a path mean the global scope.
  - `GET /processes/templates?concept_id&all`.
  - `GET /processes/templates/scopes` returns each overriding node with the number of documents its template checks.
  - `GET /processes/templates/for/{id|global}` returns the template plus `applies_to_path` and `own_versions`.
  - `GET .../for/{id}/download?kind=blank|example|schema`.
  - `POST /processes/templates/scope/{id}/clear` stops a node overriding, revalidates every document, and returns `now`.
  - `GET /processes/templates/{id|default}` and `.../download`.
  - `POST /processes/templates/preview` reads an upload of up to 10 MB, decoded as `utf-8-sig`. It is used as a schema if `looks_like_schema`; otherwise a schema is inferred from the example. Returns `{kind, schema, example, problems, suggested_name}`.
  - `POST /processes/templates` (201) takes `TemplateCreate{name, schema (alias), example, kind schema|inferred, description, make_default, concept_id}` and revalidates everything when `make_default` is set.
  - `POST /processes/templates/{id}/default` makes the template active at its scope and revalidates.
  - `DELETE /processes/templates/{id}`.
- **Usage and resolution:**
  - `GET /processes/usage?document_id&concept_id (descendants included)&subject_type&subject_id&limit≤2000`.
  - `GET /processes/resolve?goal=` previews what the process-knowledge layer would pick: `{scope, mode, message, candidates, documents (summarised), threshold}`.

## Key elements
- **`_guard`** maps errors to statuses:
  - `VocabularyError` → 409
  - `LookupError` → 404
  - `PermissionError` → 409
  - `ValueError` → 422
  - `RuntimeError` → 503
- **`_read(file)`** reads at most `PROCESS_DOC_MAX_KB*1024 + 1` bytes. The one extra byte is enough for the validator to report "too large" without buffering a huge file.

## Control flow
Most heavy work runs in `asyncio.to_thread`.

## Data, state and side effects
- The catalog concepts and links.
- The process documents, templates and usage tables (`app/process/*`).
- Mistral calls for fix and draft.
- Neo4j cleanup on delete.

## Configuration
`PROCESS_KNOWLEDGE_DEFAULT`, `PROCESS_DOC_MAX_KB` and `PROCESS_MATCH_MIN_SCORE`.

## Interactions
- Route policy:
  - recommendations need knowledge.manage;
  - `validate` and `templates/preview` need catalog.view;
  - GET needs catalog.view;
  - writes need catalog.manage.
- Builds read the documents through `app/process/pipeline.py`.

## Error handling and edge cases
See Key elements.

## Nuances and gotchas
The router prefix is `/processes`. The recommendations routes on the same prefix live in `routes/knowledge.py`.

## How to rebuild this file
The helpers, models and handlers above, keeping the id-generation rules exactly.

## Tests
`backend/tests/test_process_knowledge.py`, `test_template_context.py` and `test_recommendation_import.py`.
